clue.text: She inspires musicians, top pair leaving Blue Peter, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the remaining letters have gone wrong and must be reshuffled
the first two letters of the words Blue Peter are dropped before anything else happens

explanation.surface: A muse of music bids a tearful farewell to the long-running BBC children's programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top pair leaving' takes BL off BLUE PETER, leaving UEPETER, which 'sadly' rearranges. BLUE PETER is a long-running British children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this figure is the Muse presiding over music and lyric poetry, a source of inspiration for players.

clue.text: At uni, Jack tackles work at the usual level

parts.note: being up at university is the British phrase for studying there

indicators.note: tackles means grabs hold of, so the sailor's word wraps round the work

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, a tar
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A student, Jack, gets stuck into an assignment of ordinary standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for meeting the normal expected standard, as a golfer equalling par does.

clue.text: Rave about introducing liberal scorer

indicators.note: introducing means putting something into the rant word
about here means turned round, so the whole build is read backwards

parts.note: to rave is to rage, rant furiously

explanation.surface: A critic rants about a progressive composer being brought into the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts L into RAGE to give RAGLE; 'about' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer is one who writes musical scores, and this English composer wrote the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: European opens factories making a suite

indicators.note: opens here means the abbreviation sits inside the factories word, splitting it

parts.note: industrial plants are factories

explanation.surface: A European businessman launches factories producing a set of rooms or furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's orchestral suite in seven movements, each named for a heavenly body, is known by this title.

clue.text: Malign injection, one in tongue

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to malign
a jab is an injection
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A harmful jab given to a single patient's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language; this is a variant spelling of the language of Punjab.

clue.text: Lacking source, most plump for evidence

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, which goes missing here

parts.note: the most plump is the fattest

explanation.surface: Without a starting point, one plumps for the most likely evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plump for' looks like 'choose', but 'most plump' is the superlative of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to evidence and to bear witness to are synonyms: both mean to show something is true.

clue.text: First person in Paris, odd, clinches deal for city

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person singular

indicators.note: clinches means grips tightly, so the odd word holds the deal word

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd, peculiar
a sale is a deal

explanation.surface: A strange Frenchman closes a deal for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy city in the Middle East, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Barman's old staff filling wine store

definitions.note: a man of musical bars, a composer, rather than a pub server

indicators.note: filling means stuffing into the middle of the wine store word

parts.note: a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: The bartender's ancient stick is stuffed into the wine rack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman's' reads as a pub worker's possessive; it is 'Barman is', a man of bars, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is written in bars, so a composer such as this Russian, of Prince Igor fame, is a cryptic bar-man.

clue.text: Tune librarian ordered for last night's singalong?

definitions.note: the song sung at the Last Night of the Proms

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune is requested from a librarian for the end of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Night of the Proms is a British classical concert ending with patriotic communal singing.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriotic Arne song is a fixture of the closing Proms concert, where the audience joins in.

clue.text: Special quotation does attract him

parts.note: a tag is a short familiar quotation

explanation.surface: A special quotation says what attracts a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is not the verb but plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deer are drawn to the adult male deer in the rutting season.

clue.text: Those playing away read result elsewhere

indicators.note: elsewhere puts these letters in other places, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fans of an away team read the score in another place.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing away is British slang for being unfaithful, so cheating spouses fit.

clue.text: Fights are ultimately few and far between

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word are

explanation.surface: Fights are, in the end, rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thinly scattered and scarce is infrequent, the sense of the idiom.

clue.text: English players cross a street somewhere in New York

indicators.note: cross means the street piece lies across, between the two other pieces

parts.note: a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: An English team crosses a road somewhere in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Side is an area of Manhattan, as in the Upper and Lower districts.

clue.text: Box in odd Scottish ensemble

indicators.note: in places the box word inside the Scottish word

parts.note: orra is Scots for odd or occasional
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A box sits in a strange Scottish group.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of musicians playing together is an ensemble.

clue.text: European suspended heretic

parts.note: hung means suspended
an Arian is a follower of Arius, a heretic

explanation.surface: A European heretic is left hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a central European country is one example of a European.

clue.text: Big noise making contribution to Gaelic language

indicators.note: making contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A prominent figure helps a Celtic tongue along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big noise' looks like an important person, but here it is a loud sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic sound is a big noise.

clue.text: American in front of gallery getting on

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of gallery

explanation.surface: An American standing before a gallery is getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' looks like the definition, ageing; 'getting' is a link and 'on' means taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on drugs is taking them, so the slang sense of on matches.

clue.text: Small supporter welcomes a composer

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the support word holds a

parts.note: a truss is a supporting framework or belt

explanation.surface: A minor backer embraces a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Waltz king Johann and Richard, of Salome fame, both bear this composer surname.

clue.text: Voice witty remark about second last

parts.note: to voice is to utter

indicators.note: about means around, so the remark surrounds the second

parts.note: a mot is a witty saying, from bon mot

explanation.surface: Deliver a clever quip about coming second last.
explanation.definitionFit: Farthest or extreme in position, synonymous with the final one.

clue.text: Accolades come in a burst

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise arrives in a sudden rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal speeches or writings of high praise, the plural of a Latin-derived word for tributes.

clue.text: Second number limits disheartened opera singer

indicators.note: limits means bounds on both sides, so the two pieces sit at either end
disheartened removes the heart, the middle letter, of opera

explanation.surface: A second numbered act restricts a dispirited opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' drops the central E of OPERA to leave OPRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female voice in opera, so a type of singer.

clue.text: Hairy sailor occupies mansion

indicators.note: occupies means lives inside, so the sailor goes into the mansion

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house
OS, ordinary seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A shaggy seaman takes over a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical and zoological term for covered in soft hairs.

clue.text: Our start and our finish perhaps, short of money?

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the money letter is dropped

parts.note: burning of the body is one way our lives end

explanation.surface: Birth and death, a question of not having enough cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our start' is the Biblical making of the world; dropping M from a funeral method gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis making of the world, and of humankind, is the beginning of us all.

clue.text: In good spirits, sending out tweets?

definitions.meaning: making bird calls, as a bird does; or posting on social media

explanation.surface: A cheerful person posts on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful and making short high bird sounds are both senses of the adjective.

clue.text: Children's author nearly stood up dramatist

indicators.note: stood up, in a down entry, means read upwards, backwards
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A children's writer almost stood up a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts NESBIT to NESBI, and 'stood up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian author of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler wrote plays.

clue.text: Listener writer's defending superior concert hall

parts.note: an auditor is a hearer, one who listens

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so I'm goes round the superior letter

parts.note: the writer's is I'm, the setter saying I am
U means upper class, superior

explanation.surface: A listener says the writer is defending a superior concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a theatre or hall where the audience sits, and by extension the whole venue.

clue.text: Lover of poetry dispatches one big flyer

indicators.note: dispatches means sends away, so the one is removed

parts.note: a swain is a young lover in pastoral poetry
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A poetry fan sends off a huge plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A large water bird capable of flight, so literally a big flyer.

clue.text: A local star embarrassed about being in two pieces

parts.note: the sun is our own local star

indicators.note: about means turned round, so red is reversed

parts.note: an embarrassed face goes red

explanation.surface: A celebrity from the area blushes over being split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local star' suggests a neighbourhood celebrity; it is the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart into separate parts is the meaning of the adverb.

clue.text: Version of The Trout drops leading section

parts.note: rain is drops of water
the bow is the front part of a ship

explanation.surface: A performance of Schubert's Trout Quintet cuts its opening movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Trout' suggests Schubert's piece, but it is the fish; one kind is the rainbow trout.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of trout with iridescent colouring is a variety, or version, of the fish.
